subject: Possible biases of HMs for modelling abundance in point counts

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: Possible biases of HMs for modelling abundance in point counts
parts:
Dear all,

I am currently using hierarchical models for modelling abundance, in particular I am using simplified N-mixture 
model with distance sampling, Royle 2004 - the JAGS implementation of generalized
unmarked::gdistsamp()-like model. On point count data.

The results in many cases contradict the expert estimations 
of abundance (mostly they seem overestimated, in few cases underestimated though). Of course the expert estimation
has problems as well, but we have to be careful when intepreting the models too.
Can you recommend any source  (or your personal experience!) that would discuss possible 
biases of these models? Or, biases of using point counts for density estimation in general.

The only thing I have found is Buckland 2006 (The Auk) which connects bird movement during counting
with abundance overestimation. And of course Newson 2008 (Journal of Applied Ecology) but his findings doesn't seem very 
applicable to our case.

Thanks a lot!

Tomas

messages.author: b5ef6a364cbb7125
messages.subject: Re: Possible biases of HMs for modelling abundance in point counts
parts:
Tomas,

A useful reference might be Chandler et al. 2011 ("Inference about density and temporary immigration in unmarked populations", Ecology 92).  That paper specifically addresses availability issues and density bias in Binomial N-mixture models. Another useful reference might be Jake Laake et al.'s 2011 paper in the Journal of Ag., Bio., and Envr. Statistics, or Efford and Dawson 2009 in the Auk.  It sounds like you are estimating phi; the other issues that to mind to mind might be lack of super-population closure or relate to where observations are truncated.   Most of the (very few) papers I've read re. distance sampling seem to suggest that the problem is that failing to consider distance causes negative bias: so perhaps the expert estimations are wrong?

John
